sources.title: How to Kick or Ban Players on a Palworld Server

notes: Official docs write every command with a leading slash (/ShowPlayers) because that is the in-game admin-chat form; over RCON the slash is dropped and the bare word is sent - palworld-server-docker sends RCON "ShowPlayers" and "broadcast <msg>" through rcon-cli, and GameServerKings states the console form is 'the same commands typed without the leading slash'. Casing here follows the official docs; the server is case-insensitive in practice. Broadcast cannot carry spaces over RCON: palworld-server-docker replaces every space with an underscore before sending, and non-ASCII messages fail outright - a caller that needs real spaces should use the REST API instead. ShowPlayers returns CSV with a header row and three columns, name,playeruid,<platform>_<id>; palworld-server-docker's player_logging.sh comments the third column as (steam|ps5|gdk)_<id> and skips the header with tail -n +2, and a player still loading or in character creation shows a playeruid of 8 or 32 zeroes. SOURCES DISAGREE on the moderation identifier: the official command reference still says <SteamID>; GameServerKings says either the Steam ID or the Player UID works for Steam players and that Xbox/Game Pass/PS5/Mac players must be addressed by Player UID; BisectHosting documents /KickPlayer steam_<SteamID>; and the REST API's kick takes a 'userid' string, the same field the /players response returns. The pattern therefore accepts both the bare id and a platform-prefixed form, and it does NOT enumerate platform prefixes - only (steam|ps5|gdk) are attested anywhere I read, so the prefix group is written generically rather than as a list. The value taken straight out of the ShowPlayers third column is the recommended one to pass, but for non-Steam players GameServerKings' advice (use the Player UID, column two) is the documented fallback if a kick appears to hit nobody. Palworld also exposes a REST admin API (RESTAPIEnabled/RESTAPIPort, default 8212, HTTP Basic auth with the admin password, base path /v1/api, endpoints info/players/announce/kick/ban/unban); it is recorded here as a note rather than as the transport because RCON is the older and more widely deployed channel, but note that palworld-server-docker now logs 'RCON IS DEPRECATED AND WILL BE REMOVED IN A FUTURE RELEASE. PLEASE USE THE REST API INSTEAD.' and prefers REST, so a future revision may flip this file to rest. Setting names RCONEnabled/RCONPort/AdminPassword come from the official configuration reference, which prints no defaults; the 25575 default is from palworld-server-docker (RCON_PORT 25575). juunini/palworld-rcon implements Info, ShowPlayers, KickPlayer, BanPlayer and Broadcast but has no UnBanPlayer method - UnBanPlayer rests on the official reference plus GameServerKings. No motd command exists.
